answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with randomly paid attestation: every epoch, a small random sample of identities is audited by jurors who stake coins on their verdict. A fake that survives one audit may still be caught in the next, so its expected lifetime spirals toward zero, while audit costs stay small because only a few are checked. Honest agents treat the rare audit as an oasis of trust in a desert of copies, and a relic identity that passes audit after audit earns a reputation no fresh forgery can buy.
